observation.visible_scene: A single pink spherical ball positioned in front of a plain off‑white wall, hovering above a light wooden mat/floor. The ball stays roughly centered horizontally across the whole excerpt; the wall and mat are static.
visible_changes: The ball starts at an elevated position and moves downward toward the mat over the first several frames.
Around t≈0.23 s the ball meets the mat and visibly deforms into a flattened, wider 'squash' shape.
It then returns to a round shape and lifts off the mat, rising to a mid‑height.
For a long stretch (roughly t≈0.3–0.9 s) the ball remains airborne at a nearly steady height above the mat, with little apparent vertical change between samples.
Near t≈1.0 s the ball contacts the mat a second time and squashes again.
After that second contact it regains its round form and rises only slightly, ending the excerpt a short distance above the mat.
A soft shadow on the mat tracks the ball, appearing/fading as the ball's height changes.
Because the wall and mat show no displacement, the observed motion belongs to the ball, not to camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or prior motion that placed the ball high in frame 1 is not shown.
What happens after the final frame (whether the ball keeps bouncing or settles) is not shown.
uncertain_details: The exact vertical path between sampled frames is approximate; the airborne interval looks almost constant in height, so small per‑frame rises/falls cannot be resolved.
Whether the horizontal position is perfectly fixed or drifts by a few pixels is hard to judge from the stills.
The apparent long 'hover' could reflect a slow apex region or a low‑amplitude motion; the frames alone do not disambiguate this.
